name: photon-examples
description: A focused set of teaching photons that show one Photon capability at a time.

photons.name: walkthrough
photons.description:
Photon Walkthrough

An interactive step-by-step guide to building photons. Every demo is a real method on this photon — zero external dependencies. The slides show code for named classes, but the live UI calls these methods.
photons.author: Unknown
photons.label: Walkthrough
photons.summary: A guided first photon that explains the file, methods, and outputs.

photons.name: discoverable
photons.description:
Discoverable Service

Demonstrates Server Cards and A2A Agent Cards. Both card types are auto-generated from the same photon metadata — rich docblocks, @stateful tag, and method descriptions map directly to MCP Server Card tools and A2A Agent Card skills.
photons.author: Unknown
photons.label: Discoverable
photons.summary: Shows how metadata and method descriptions make a photon easy for agents to use.

photons.name: context-aware
photons.description:
Context-Aware Photon

Demonstrates bidirectional state exposure where frontend widget state flows into photon methods via this._clientState.
photons.author: Unknown
photons.label: Context Aware
photons.summary: Demonstrates runtime context and environment-aware behavior.

photons.name: render-showcase
photons.description:
Render Showcase

Demonstrates photon.render() — how custom UIs can use auto UI format renderers (table, gauge, chart, etc.) without building everything from scratch.

Each method returns sample data in a shape that a specific format renderer understands. The custom UI dashboard calls photon.render(container, data, format) to visualize them.
photons.author: Unknown
photons.label: Render Showcase
photons.summary: Returns rich UI output so chat clients and Beam can render more than text.

photons.name: input-showcase
photons.description:
Input Showcase

Demonstrates all input format types in the Photon auto-UI. Each method showcases a different input widget.
photons.author: Unknown
photons.label: Input Showcase
photons.summary: Demonstrates form inputs and interactive parameters for agent-driven workflows.

photons.name: ag-ui-showcase
photons.description:
AG-UI Event Showcase

Demonstrates how photon yields map to AG-UI protocol events. String yields become TEXT_MESSAGE events, progress yields become STEP events, and return values become STATE_SNAPSHOT events.
photons.author: Unknown
photons.label: AG-UI Showcase
photons.summary: Shows agent UI events and structured interaction patterns.

photons.name: pizza-shop
photons.description:
Pizza Shop - AI Pizza Ordering Assistant

Demonstrates the AI+Human transaction workflow for food ordering: 1. AI suggests pizzas based on preferences 2. Human selects and customizes items 3. Human reviews cart and confirms order 4. System processes order with delivery info
photons.author: Photon Team
photons.label: Pizza Shop
photons.summary: A playful storefront example for embedded app flows and state transitions.

photons.name: background-job
photons.description:
Background Job Processor

Demonstrates MCP Tasks for fire-and-forget async operations. Designed for tasks/create — the client gets a task ID immediately and polls tasks/get for progress and results.
photons.author: Unknown
photons.label: Background Job
photons.summary: Demonstrates long-running work and progress updates.

photons.name: deploy-pipeline
photons.description:
Deploy Pipeline

Demonstrates persistent approvals for destructive operations. Approval confirmations survive page navigation and server restarts.
photons.author: Unknown
photons.label: Deploy Pipeline
photons.summary: Shows streaming deployment stages as an agent-friendly workflow.

photons.name: observable
photons.description:
Observable Computation Service

Demonstrates OpenTelemetry GenAI instrumentation. When @opentelemetry/api is installed, all tool calls produce gen_ai.tool.call spans with standardized attributes. Without the package, everything works with zero overhead.
photons.author: Unknown
photons.label: Observable
photons.summary: Demonstrates observable state changes that clients can follow.
